summary: Discovery call to map integration paths for Redwood hosted vs dedicated deployments. Main focus: SDKs and LangChain/LlamaIndex support, gateway/proxy placement, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Customer leans toward dedicated for predictable latency and compliance but wants a path to a hosted pilot. Next steps: share pricing, security docs, and sample integrations; run a technical benchmark with SE and customer infra.
topics: Rate limiting, quotas, and burst handling
Observability hooks, tracing, and token-level cost breakdown
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, I'll kick us off. Today we want to understand your integration needs and figure out hosted vs dedicated vs private, and what a pilot would look like.
[00:18] Marta (Cedar CTO): Thanks Alex. We got a brief note from your AE, wanted to see how it fits with our stack. I'm Marta, CTO. Ben and Leah are on to cover SRE and ML.
[00:30] Ben (Cedar SRE): Hi. Our priorities are predictable latency, multi-region routing, and simple observability.
[00:40] Priya (Redwood SE): Great. Quick intros: I'm Priya, SE. I usually help with SDKs, LangChain adapters, and benchmarks. Jordan will hop in for infra specifics.
[00:50] Leah (ML Eng): We mostly use LangChain and LlamaIndex in our pipelines today, for retrieval-augmented generation. Key question: do you provide first-class adapters or do we need to wrap the HTTP API ourselves?
[01:10] Priya (Redwood SE): Good question. We have official SDKs in Python and JavaScript and maintained LangChain + LlamaIndex connectors. The SDK includes streaming, function/tool calls, and a small adapter example for LlamaIndex. There's a quickstart repo I can share.
[01:30] Marta: Okay. How about rate limits and quotas? We have spikes from nightly batches and unpredictable burst from the app.
[01:45] Alex: For hosted, we have per-key quotas and soft rate limits, and you can request burst increases. For Dedicated, you reserve capacity — GPU pools — so quota isn't the same model, it's throughput-backed. Priya: Dedicated avoids short-term throttling because you have dedicated pods.
[02:10] Ben: If we go dedicated, how does traffic routing work? We have an API gateway on-prem, and some services in AWS. Can we put Redwood behind our proxy or do we need to call your gateway directly?
[02:28] Jordan (Solutions Eng): You can do either. For Private deployments we can run in your VPC or on-prem; for Dedicated you can route via a secure egress from your gateway to our endpoints or set up a customer-facing proxy. There are tradeoffs — if you insist on all egress through your proxy you'll add latency but keep control.
[02:50] Omar (Sec): A couple compliance Qs: KMS integration, audit logs, and retention. Do you integrate with customer KMS/HSM?
[03:02] Priya: Yes, for Private deployments we support customer KMS. For Dedicated we offer KMS integrations too; for hosted we manage encryption at rest but we can support customer-managed keys in some enterprise contracts. Audit logs and token-level billing are in our Console for Dedicated/Private.
[03:25] Leah: On the LangChain side, do you preserve streaming and delta tokens so we can compute token cost per chain step?
[03:35] Priya: Streaming is supported in SDK and LangChain connector; we expose token counts and cost metadata in responses and the Console gives per-route breakdowns. There are edge cases where transcriptions of system messages get counted — sometimes our auto-transcription writes something odd — but we show the raw token counts.
[03:55] Marta: We're sensitive to data residency and also want to avoid sending PII to a third-party hosted service if possible.
[04:05] Alex: That's common. For that you have two options: Dedicated in a region close to your users with strict retention, or Private (VPC/on-prem) where the control plane is customer-managed and you can enforce no external egress.
[04:22] Ben: For benchmarking, what do you need from us?
[04:28] Priya: A sample traffic trace — QPS, payload sizes, average tokens per request, burst patterns, and SLO targets (p95 latency). We'll run a dedicated pilot that mirrors your traffic and can test both hosted and dedicated variants.
[04:45] Marta: Timeline: we'd like a pilot in early Sept, roughly two weeks long, and then a production decision by mid-September. Is that feasible?
[04:55] Alex: Yes, doable. We'll aim to have a pilot proposal within a week.
[05:05] Ben: How do you recommend integrating with LangChain? Are there specific classes or is it just raw HTTP callouts?
[05:13] Priya: The LangChain connector implements an LLM wrapper that maps to our streaming and function-calling semantics. For LlamaIndex, there's a small adapter that manages the retriever call and streaming generation. We'll share the notebook. Some customers prefer to pin model versions to avoid drift.
[05:32] Leah: Model pinning is important — we need deterministic behavior for evals.
[05:36] Priya: You can pin model versions and keep a rollback policy. The Console shows model versions and you can configure canaries or A/B splits.
[05:45] Marta: About observability: we use Datadog and Lightstep tracing. Can we get spans or traces from Redwood calls?
[05:56] Jordan: We expose tracing hooks and can emit OpenTelemetry spans to your collector for Dedicated and Private. For hosted there's an out-of-the-box webhook and logs export, but direct OTLP ingestion is available in enterprise plans.
[06:15] Omar: And the token-level cost — can we get per-request costlines? That's a blocker for chargeback.
[06:24] Alex: Yes, Console exposes per-request token counts and cost; for Dedicated you can also export detailed logs with token breakdowns. We'll include sample CSV exports.
[06:35] Ben: On the networking side, does Redwood support mTLS and IP allowlists for endpoints?
[06:42] Priya: We support mTLS for Private and Dedicated. For hosted, we do allowlists and per-key controls, and can negotiate mTLS in enterprise contracts.
[06:54] Marta: I keep hearing about KV cache and batching — how much of a difference do those make for latency and cost?
[07:03] Priya: Automatic KV/prefix caching can cut token ops dramatically for chat-style workloads by reusing cached KV cache across requests; batching reduces per-token overhead for high-throughput workloads but increases tail latency a bit. Our Optimize tooling analyzes your traces and suggests batching profiles and quantization to meet cost/latency tradeoffs.
[07:28] Leah: Speaking of quantization, do you support 4-bit quant models on Dedicated?
[07:33] Priya: We support quantized variants where applicable and pick kernels optimized for the hardware. You can choose model profiles that trade a small quality delta for large cost improvements for high-volume workloads.
[07:45] Ben: If we start with hosted to move quickly, what's the path to migrate to Dedicated without code changes?
[07:53] Alex: The API and SDKs are the same across modes. For Dedicated you'd adjust the endpoint and potentially auth creds, but your LangChain / LlamaIndex wrappers should work with minimal changes. We can provide a migration checklist.
[08:08] Marta: Can you run a short POC that demonstrates the LangChain workflow end-to-end with our retrievers? We're concerned about connector compat and whether function calls will map cleanly.
[08:20] Priya: Absolutely. Typical POC: 1) we get a sample dataset and retriever config, 2) we run a week of simulated traffic or a short dedicated pilot, 3) we produce latency/cost report and a list of recommended configs (batching, cache TTLs, quant profile).
[08:39] Leah: Any gotchas with LlamaIndex? We saw some missing metadata in streaming replies with another vendor.
[08:47] Priya: Occasionally streaming chunk boundaries can be different; our connector attempts to preserve metadata and function-call tokens. We'll include end-to-end tests in the sample notebook.
[08:58] Ben: About quotas, if we use hosted, how are limits enforced? Per API key or account?
[09:05] Alex: Per API key and account. You can set sub-keys for teams and have different quotas and rate limits. There's also rate-limit headers so your gateway can fallback gracefully.
[09:17] Marta: In terms of price, what's the approximate unit cost delta between hosted and dedicated reserve?
[09:23] Alex: Hosted is pay-as-you-go; Dedicated usually lowers per-token unit cost for heavy steady workloads because you're buying capacity. We'll send a pricing sheet showing examples.
[09:35] Omar: Anything in the contract around data deletion guarantees for hosted? We need to ensure transcripts and logs are deleted after retention TTL.
[09:44] Priya: We can include contractual retention and deletion clauses. For Dedicated and Private you control retention TTLs directly.
[09:55] Jordan: Quick note on gateway/proxy: if you want to run a local gateway that fans requests to Redwood, we recommend putting a lightweight proxy that handles auth and routing while keeping TLS to Redwood endpoints intact to avoid MITM issues and preserve tracing.
[10:12] Ben: Does that mean we can add our own rate-limiting at our gateway and Redwood will enforce a second layer?
[10:19] Priya: Yes, dual-layer rate limiting works well: your gateway enforces per-customer rules and Redwood enforces per-key quotas. We'll show header based backoff signals.
[10:30] Leah: For the pilot, what success metrics should we define? We're thinking p95 latency under 220ms for short prompts, sustained throughput of 200 QPS, and cost per 1k tokens under X.
[10:42] Alex: Those are good starters. We'll help you formalize SLOs, and align the benchmark to measure p50/p95/p99 and token-level billing.
[10:55] Marta: Who's the point-of-contact on Redwood side to move infra things forward?
[11:00] Alex: Me for commercial and Priya for SE/benchmarking and Jordan for infra.
[11:07] Omar: A couple quick security clarifications: Do you rotate credentials automatically? And is there support for SAML/SSO for Console?
[11:16] Priya: We support SAML/SSO and RBAC on Console. Credential rotation can be automated and we integrate with your secret stores in Private/Dedicated setups.
[11:28] Ben: Any suggested observability hooks for Datadog?
[11:33] Jordan: We emit logs and metrics; for Dedicated we can add OTLP spans. For Datadog, we provide a sample dashboard template with token counts, latency percentiles, error rates, and cost per route.
[11:48] Leah: Can you show a short demo of SDK code?
[11:52] Priya: Sure, I'll paste a short Python snippet after the call — but gist is: import redwood, create client with key, use langchain adapter or call client.stream().
[12:05] Alex: Okay, thinking about blockers — Marta, is legal or procurement needed before a pilot?
[12:12] Marta: We'll need procurement review and a security checklist. Procurement can sign a short pilot agreement if the terms are standard.
[12:22] Alex: We'll send a pilot agreement template and security pack.
[12:28] Ben: One last question: any limitations around long context and KV cache persistence across sessions?
[12:36] Priya: KV cache is session-aware; it persists for configurable TTLs on Dedicated/Private. For hosted we have shorter TTL defaults but can extend for enterprise. Very long contexts are best handled via retrievers rather than pushing huge prompt windows.
[12:50] Marta: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[12:54] Alex: Recap — we'll send pricing, security docs, quickstart repo, and the LangChain/LlamaIndex sample notebook. Priya will run an internal dry-run with a sample dataset. Ben will provide traffic patterns. We'll schedule the deep-dive around Aug 13.
[13:12] Marta: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[13:15] Alex: Thanks — we'll follow up.

Notes: transcript contains filler and occasional mis-transcribed tokens; speaker labels approximate, timestamps every ~30-90s. Some vendor/product names may be slightly misspelled in auto-transcription.
